context: Kenji shows Ren how the office works on his first day.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.style: Open, genuine warmth. A slight lean-in on the name. No performance—just real invitation. Steady pace, soft on the welcome. The ease of someone who actually means it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: よろしくお願いします。
lines.style: Respectful but not stiff. A small breath before speaking. Earnest without over-reaching. Clear, present, receptive. The kind of sincerity that comes from paying attention to what's being offered.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 名刺、用意した、これ、使って。
lines.en: I've prepared some business cards for you. Here—use these.
lines.style: Practical warmth. A beat of presentation, handing something real over. Matter-of-fact kindness. No fuss, just the gesture that says 'you belong here already.'

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。
lines.style: Formal politeness with genuine gratitude underneath. Not rushed. A small nod lives in the voice. Respectful of what was just given, what it signals.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.en: Ask about anything—no question too small. I mean it.
lines.style: Softness here. An invitation, not an obligation. The reassurance of someone who remembers what it's like to be new. Slightly slower on 'anything,' letting him know the door is actually open.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 頑張ります、皆と一緒に。
lines.en: I'll do my best. We're all in this together.
lines.style: A small brightness comes in. Still earnest, but with the note of commitment. Not performing confidence, just quiet resolve. The slight lift at the end—'together'—makes it real.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.en: That gives me real confidence. Thank you.
lines.style: Genuine warmth meeting gratitude. A slight soften on the close—this moment matters to him too. Not overstated. The quiet contentment of someone who just welcomed someone into something real.
